demos.name: Unregistered Scene Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
I wrote most of this game’s code myself, with AI assistance on a small portion. I designed its architecture, built the systems used across the game, and wrote most of the game-specific logic.

The art, music, and sound effects were made with the help of generative AI. I developed the characters and the game’s world, set the overall mood and visual style, and described the content and composition I wanted for the images. I also selected and revised the AI-generated results. The promotional images and concept trailers on the Steam store page were also made with the help of generative AI.

I wrote the entire story, directed every scene, and designed all player interactions. I also designed each level’s core concept, design intent, techniques, and pacing. I set the constraints and used a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) solver to generate a vast pool of candidate levels in advance, rather than having generative AI produce them directly. I playtested and selected from the candidates, refining the constraints along the way until I arrived at the final levels. Each level has exactly one solution and can be solved without guessing.

Translations into languages other than Chinese currently use AI assistance.

If any of this still bothers you, I understand. If you give the game a try, I believe the best parts of the experience come from a bit of old-fashioned craft, even if it’s a little rough around the edges.

— The Developer

This game uses live generative AI through the Anthropic Claude API during specific gameplay scenes. Optional English speech for eligible generated N.E.K.O. replies is provided through ElevenLabs.

In the demo, AI is used for:
- N.E.K.O. free-talk, where the player can ask the ship AI limited in-character questions.
- A Chapter 2 persuasion/debate challenge, where the model evaluates player text and returns a structured result.
- Optional English voice generation for eligible N.E.K.O. replies, including recap conversations.

In the full game, AI is used for additional bounded minigames, including conversation, persuasion, tactical planning, insult-comedy judging, and legal-argument judging.

The AI generates short text responses or structured JSON gameplay judgments, and optional English speech of eligible displayed replies. It does not generate images, video, executable code, or multiplayer/user-to-user content during gameplay.

demos.name: Cozy Necromancy Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
A small language model (Google's Gemma 3 270M) runs entirely on the player's computer, with no network connection. It writes short lines of villager small talk, the ritual oracle's one- or two-sentence hint after a failed ritual, and routine filler records in the in-game archive, and it chooses which of our pre-written dialogue lines fits the moment.

Guardrails: the player never types to the model — there is no text input anywhere in the game. Every prompt is a fixed template we wrote, filled in from game state such as a character's name, the time of day and the current quest. Output is short by construction (hard token caps, and lines over a few words are cut or discarded); lines that read as narration, stage directions or an assistant speaking are rejected; dialogue choices are constrained to our own authored lines. Any failure falls back to written lines. Players can turn the model off in Settings, and the game plays identically on written lines alone.

demos.name: Veil of Time Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
Veil of Time is a hand-built game. The maps, the writing, the music, the interface, and the game design are all human work. Generative AI was used in five specific places, each reviewed and finished by hand:

1. Voice acting. Every line of dialogue and every in-game book can be spoken aloud (3,707 voice clips), synthesized with ElevenLabs from the game's own written script. We chose this so the story stays open to players with low vision or reading difficulties, and to younger players who are not fast readers yet. A voice cast of this size would otherwise be out of reach for a small studio. No performance was cloned from a real person without licence.

2. Character and bestiary portraits, generated from the game's original hand-made sprites and finished by hand.

3. Some character sprites and the party's battle animation sheets, produced with AI assistance from the project's own hand-drawn art, then hand-corrected and palette-locked.

4. The intro and outro cinematic stills, the title screen, and the store key art.

5. Ambient critters and butterflies, converted from hand-made source art.

Everything else you see, read, and hear was made by people.

Policy on the Use of Generative AI Technology in Our Titles
HUGA INC. (hereinafter referred to as "the Company") actively adopts and utilizes generative AI technology—including code assistance tools for development efficiency and image generation—in our titles. This is positioned as part of our development process to pursue new possibilities of artistic expression and high productivity in small-scale indie game development.

In utilizing AI technology, the Company strictly adheres to the following compliance and development standards:

■ Compliance with Laws and Intellectual Property Rights
Our development process complies with the Copyright Act of Japan (including the provisions for information analysis under Article 30-4) as well as the laws and regulations of relevant countries. Generative AI tools are used strictly within legally permitted boundaries.

■ Adherence to Distribution Platform Guidelines
We strictly comply with the disclosure obligations and various guidelines regarding generative AI established by Steam and other distribution platforms, ensuring appropriate information disclosure and proper registration processes.

■ Establishment of Creative Direction as a Proprietary Product
All AI-generated assets are integrated into our games only after undergoing our strict creative direction, editing, processing, and reconstruction within the overall game design. Our products do not rely on mere automated output.

The Company positions the proactive adoption of new technologies to deliver next-generation entertainment as a core innovation strategy for an indie developer.

Please note that while the Company closely monitors the ongoing social and ethical debates surrounding AI technology, we conduct our business lawfully based on current regulations and platform rules. Therefore, we do not issue individual statements or respond to inquiries regarding legal interpretations or related debates. Thank you for your understanding.

No images or story are generated live while you play
Dialogue, events, and localization were written and proofread by the development team—not produced dynamically by AI during gameplay
How it was made
Art was generated on the developer’s machine using image-generation tools (SwarmUI / Z-Image Turbo), guided by fixed style and character prompts. Outputs were manually selected and post-processed (e.g. cutout, compositing, resizing) before import into the Godot project. Your copy contains fixed assets only; gameplay does not trigger new AI generation.

If you prefer to judge the visual style first, please review the screenshots and trailer on this store page.

Every creative and technical decision was made by the developer, and all AI-generated output was reviewed and curated before inclusion.
No AI is invoked during gameplay. The game runs entirely offline and makes no calls to external AI services.
This is a parody experiment, and the use of AI is part of the experiment itself. We disclose it here so you can decide whether that approach is interesting to you.

The in-game 2D visual assets and the 2D upgrade and ability icons began as generated

reworked them in bulk with custom scripts, and intends to replace them with work

demos.name: Forged Cards Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
Forged Cards is a passion project, built by one person. I'm not a game studio, I'm a single developer who fell in love with an idea for a deck-builder where you build the cards and set out to make it real.
Games like this usually take a team. Modern AI development tools are a big part of how one person was able to build something at this scope. I used AI coding assistants to help me build and iterate on the game's systems, AI image generation for the art, and AI-generated sound effects, all of it reviewed, edited, and shaped by me to fit the world I wanted to create. Every card, every enemy, every choice about how this game looks and feels came from a person (and some close friends) who cared about getting it right.
I'm being upfront about this because I think you deserve to know how the thing you're playing was made. Forged Cards exists because these tools let one person build a game that otherwise would have stayed an idea in a notebook.

demos.name: More Than A Woman Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
We use generative AI for our music, and only for the music. Every track goes through days of human refinement, shaping, and polishing so it actually feels like it belongs in the world. 

All the lyrics, the emotional beats, cues for when a song should rise or fall are all written by us. We wanted the soundtrack to match the heart of each scene, not just fill space. If you want a taste of how it all comes together, you can hear it in our trailer.

We chose AI‑assisted music because licensing tracks for adult‑focused stories just isn’t possible with any great range or diversity in music  whilst also allowing us to give real musical direction to our scenes. 

This approach lets us create original music that fits the tone of the story without compromising anything else.

demos.name: Set the Record Straight Demo
demos.ai_disclosure: The game's period artwork was created with OpenAI's image generation: character portraits, the document plates and photographs on the desk, the paper stocks and document chrome the pages are printed on, and the background textures behind the game. Every one of them was directed, reviewed and composited by hand. Some diagrams were authored as SVG with OpenAI Codex. The store page art is composited from the same artwork. These assets were reviewed before release for originality and likeness. The game's written content, meaning the documents the player searches and reads and the text of the interface, is authored by the developer. Where a passage began as a draft produced with a large language model, it was cut, rewritten and checked by hand before it entered the game. No text is generated while the game runs. Sound effects and the ambient bed are produced by a deterministic synthesis program (oscillators, filtered noise and math-based DSP), not by a generative-AI audio model and from no sampled or library audio. Fonts, engine and runtime are non-AI third-party components under their own licenses (see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt).

Google Gemini - concept art and texture reference
ACE-Step - original music tracks

The music and sound effects were generated with Suno. Voice recordings were performed by the creator.

The game itself is a person's work: the rules, the mechanics, the economy and the balance decisions were designed by hand over many revisions, with AI used as a collaborator rather than an author. The physical board game came first.

A short looping background video was generated the same way and ships pre-rendered in the build. The music, including the gramophone's record, and most of the sound effects were pre-generated with AI music and sound tools and then selected, trimmed and mixed by the developer; the remaining cues are synthesized by code. The store page's capsule and library art is built from the same pre-generated plates. The narrative text is human-AI co-written under the author's direction and human-edited; the story, the simulation and the game design are the author's. Everything ships pre-rendered in the build - the game generates nothing live during play. No real people are depicted; every guest, room and document in the game is fictional.

AI is also used for tasks such as integrating graphics, music and beat analysis, and translating content. AI can complete time-consuming tasks within minutes that would otherwise take a human several hours.

No jobs are being replaced or put at risk through the use of AI in this project. This “crazy game” was still made with lots of love by humans. An AI probably would not have come up with a game idea like this anyway.

demos.ai_disclosure:
We don’t particularly like using AI.

Unfortunately, we are a small indie studio made of programmers and designers who are currently somewhere between “making a game” and “having existential crises”.

So, for now, we use AI to help us with some parts of our daily work and to bring some of our music, ideas, and inspirations to life.

But don’t worry, we haven’t handed over the steering wheel to the robots just yet.

Our project, its identity, and its originality are still created and directed by us. AI is simply one of the tools helping us survive the development process while our budget is busy pretending it doesn’t exist.

As soon as we have the resources to replace AI with our own human made work, we absolutely intend to do so.

Until then, we’re just a bunch of indie developers trying to make something cool before our refrigerators become purely decorative objects.

demos.name: Spell Death Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
Spell Death is a game about a city that stopped reading, and it was made with AI tools. Here is exactly where.

Mine, not AI:
- The design, the systems and the balance. 10+ years of making games and 30 years of building decks.
- The dictionary: a human-made list of about 196,000 words.
- Your words. Nothing is generated while you play: no suggestions, no autocomplete, and there never will be.

AI-assisted:
- Illustrations: made with image models, then picked, retouched and composed by hand.
- Music: made with an AI music tool, directed by me.
- Sound effects: most are synthesised from code; a few come from the same music tool.
- Code and some text: drafted with an AI assistant, then edited and tested by me.

The line I hold, for me and for the game: a tool is fine, a proxy is not. The machine can draw a street. It doesn't get to do your reading, your thinking or your spelling.

How is Generative AI used in this game?
Toxic Dating Simulator utilizes cutting-edge generative AI technologies to elevate its interactive cinematic storytelling.

Voice Acting (ElevenLabs): All character dialogues and Atakan's chaotic inner monologues are voiced using advanced AI-powered emotion-tagging technologies. This delivers high-fidelity voice lines capturing sarcasm, anger, or flirtatious tones with professional actor-level depth.

Visuals & Animation (Kling AI): The facial expressions, eye contact, and reactive behaviors of the female characters sitting across the cafe table are generated using advanced AI video tools.

Music: All context-dependent songs (electro, pop, or fantasy) playing on the post-date score screen are composed via AI tools, with all lyrics entirely written by the developer.

demos.name: Dust & Diamonds Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
Dust & Diamonds is a 100% solo project.

The idea for this game came to me a few days after my son was born — my first child. I was celebrating with my cousin and bet him I could build something like Motherload in two weeks. As you've probably guessed, I lost that bet spectacularly. I'm writing this almost a year later, and my son turns one in a few days.

I have a degree in computer game engineering, but I live in a small town with no game studios — so I drive a pallet jack around a warehouse by day and build this game after hours. I can't afford to hire an artist or a composer. To bring this world to life at all, I turned to generative AI tools. I'm not going to hide that.

How does the game use AI?

Graphics (2D): A significant portion of the visual assets — character portraits, environment elements, buildings — was generated using AI, then manually retouched, edited, and assembled by me in the engine into a cohesive style with a parallax system.

Music and sound: The musical tracks in the game were generated by AI. Fittingly, this ties directly into the game's lore — the "Relics of the Old World" (our 21st century) collected by the goblins are canonically works created by AI before the great cataclysm, carrying the lost wisdom of humanity.

What's mine in this game is the design: how the economy works, how water behaves in a flooded shaft, when a ceiling collapses, what the old man says across the counter. I came up with each of these systems, wrote them out, tested them, and reworked them a dozen times until they behaved the way I wanted.

I'm just a regular guy who had an idea for a game about digging in the dirt and was stubborn enough to see it through. Thank you for your understanding and support.

demos.name: Phroller - Free Version
demos.ai_disclosure:
As with most VTT systems, users are welcome to import assets made anywhere. Phroller makes it easier than ever. You can just drag the image or model files into the VTT directly from your browser or file system!

I want to encourage supporting real artists where we can though. As such I do my best to collaborate with real creatives on the vast Phroller libraries. Each one of the assets in the library has a field showing the artist behind it. If you like their work, please consider checking them out. Many of them are open for commissions as well! However, I cannot guarantee that assets or part of those assets were created with no AI use at all. A large amount of the assets are made before 2022 though, so we should be safe there.

While I do my best to make Phroller as user friendly as possible, it does still require a ton of instructions and manuals. Frontier models are used to keep some of the text up to date across rapid early access development. Sorry if it sounds robotic!

demos.name: Demon Rising Demo
demos.ai_disclosure:
Demon Rising uses generative AI for part of its content:
Live-generated narrative — The game includes a local AI language model that runs fully offline on your PC; no internet connection is required and no data is sent anywhere. During play it generates dynamic dialogue for your demon officers, war-council debates, prisoner interrogations and boss encounters, keeping conversations varied across runs. All generated text is constrained by the game's prompts to in-game characters and situations and is bounded by built-in safeguards. If the AI model is unavailable, the game automatically falls back to hand-written dialogue, so the full game is playable either way.
Pre-generated artwork — Some character portraits and illustrations were created with the help of AI image-generation tools, then selected and edited by the developer.
All AI-assisted content is curated and reviewed by the developer.

demos.ai_disclosure:
Hi! I’m a solo indie developer working on this game during my free time outside of daily life.

To bring this project to life with limited time and resources, I used AI tools to assist parts of the development process, such as brainstorming, early prototypes, draft writing, and iteration support.
However, the core game design, gameplay systems, story structure, balancing, and final implementation were all personally planned, edited, and integrated by me.

AI is a tool that helps me turn ideas into something playable—it does not replace the creative decisions behind this game.
I know people may have different opinions about AI, so I want to be transparent about it.

Thank you for playing and supporting my work.
I hope you enjoy exploring this broken, virus-corrupted world.

demos.name: s[TOR-Y]telling: Closed Loop Demo
demos.ai_disclosure: s[TOR-Y]telling uses large language models to generate text-based character interactions and narrative responses during gameplay. Players can run the included Llama model locally on compatible hardware, or choose optional Cloud AI.Technical Implementation & Privacy: Local AI generation runs on the player’s device and supports offline single-player. Cloud AI requires an internet connection and uses credits. In Cloud mode, prompts and relevant conversation context are sent through a relay operated by Curious Biped to external AI providers via OpenRouter for generation and content safety checks.Safety & Moderation: We have implemented a multi-layered safety strategy to ensure a safe experience:Model-Level Guardrails: The included local model is an Instruct model with built-in safety measures. Cloud AI uses external models with additional content safety checks performed by our relay.System-Level Directives: All prompts include an additional safety layer to prevent sexual violence, pedophilia, minor abuse/exploitation, explicit sexual behavior, or hate speech.Gameplay Integration: While the primary Visual Novel is hand-authored, the results of your sandbox evaluations influence the story's trajectory. The AI serves as a tool for narrative exploration, bridging the gap between open-ended analysis and cinematic storytelling.Generative AI was also used in the process of creating the game static assets (images, text, and music).

demos.ai_disclosure:
Static art assets (store-page capsules, in-game card art, in-game icons) and audio placeholders are generated via Replicate (Google Nano Banana Pro for image, Lyria-2 / AudioGen for audio) using human-authored prompts. Outputs are reviewed by the developer before shipping. No live AI generation occurs during gameplay; all assets are baked at build time.

I would like to pay for human assets, but I am moving fast. In the same way that AI turned 12 months of dev time into 2, it also affected how I skinned the MVP. This is best for communicating intention, and I can polish it with human art if there is traction.
